text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- No fewer than 15 people killed in a village clash in central Nigeria.
- The cut in crude oil allocation to refineries, to 250,000 bpd from 300,000 bpd, has been fingered by some sources as the real cause of the current fuel scarcity.

- Security presence is tightened in the southern oil city of Warri to ensure there is no further breach of the peace or blockage of waterways after recent ethnic clashes and hostage-taking, which temporarily cut oil production by Royal Dutch/Shell.
- "Vision 2010" economic think-tank hopes that by June it will begin working on a draft of its final report.
- Three new deputy governors of the central bank are soon to be appointed to replace those currently serving.
- General manager of southeastern Anambra State Oil Palm Agency says local farmers are being encouraged to plant improved varieties of trees to increase palm oil production.
- Oil minister Dan Etete says the oil sector needs improved funding if regular local supplies are to be ensured.
- Ministers of communications and industry suggest that privatisation may be the tonic that is needed to revitalise the public sector.
- Nigerian Agricultural Cooperative Bank prepares to recover an estimated three billion naira owed by customers.
- British American Insurance Company sets up task force to work out a blue print on how to sustain operations and evolve ways of reflating the company's low financial base.

- Oil Minister Etete pledges that more Nigerians will benefit from marginal oil fields. He said the fields are now being retrieved from multinational joint-venture partners who have shown no sign of interest in them over the past 10 years.
